hyps.why: Replacing a removed direct edge to the output with a conv restores connectivity and capacity, a bigger gain than replacing other ops.
Edge 5 is the only route from node 2 to the output, so adding a conv over none gains a lot.
Replacing none with a conv on a node-1 to output edge adds capacity and connectivity.
Edge 0 is the sole input to node 1, so a conv over none activates that whole branch.
Removing a strong conv edge costs more accuracy than removing a weak op.
Deleting a conv on the node-2 to output edge loses more than deleting a weak op.
Diminishing returns: a strong direct conv path already exists, so an extra conv helps less.
A skip is redundant when a conv already links input to output.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 cannot reach the output, so improving edge 2 is wasted.
With edge 4 removed, node 1 has a weaker route onward, so a conv on edge 0 contributes less.
